findings.issue: apiFetch caches the promise forever; a non-OK response or network error resolves to null and is cached, so a transient API failure permanently renders a real resource as Not found until the process restarts.
findings.suggestion: Cache only successful responses — on failure, delete the key so the next call retries (or add a short TTL for failures).

findings.issue: The 250 ms debounce timer is never cleaned up; if the user types and navigates to a Pokémon card within the window, the pending setTimeout calls navigate() after the Home component unmounted, yanking them back to /?q=….
findings.suggestion: Add onCleanup(() => clearTimeout(searchTimer)) in the Home component.

findings.issue: The search input is bound to the server-derived value d().q; keystrokes typed while the debounced fetch is in flight can be overwritten when the response lands.
findings.suggestion: Make the input uncontrolled (defaultValue) or only write the value when the element is not focused.

findings.issue: The Level Up table's default sort compares level only, so moves sharing a level fall back to API order instead of name order, contrary to the spec ('by level, then move name').
findings.suggestion: Add a secondary compare on moveEn (a.moveEn.localeCompare(b.moveEn)) after the level compare.

findings.issue: Selects use per-<option> selected attributes instead of a value prop; a bogus query value (e.g. ?type=xyz) leaves the control showing nothing while the filter silently doesn't apply, so the UI disagrees with the URL.
findings.suggestion: Bind value on the <select> and render a disabled/selected placeholder when the URL value isn't in the list.

findings.issue: There is no ErrorBoundary anywhere; a server-function transport error or serialization failure leaves the Suspense area blank with no user-facing fallback.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the root (or route content) in an ErrorBoundary with a simple fallback page.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemonRefs accepts an `extra` callback that no caller uses — the ability page attaches the hidden flag separately at data.js:398-405 — leaving speculative generality and a confusing dangling comment.
findings.suggestion: Drop the `extra` parameter and let callers decorate the returned cards, as the ability page already does.

findings.issue: Hash anchoring is handled only in onMount; changing the Game select navigates to ?game=…#moves but nothing scrolls, and the section markup duplicates Section.jsx to attach the ref.
findings.suggestion: Extend Section with a ref/anchor forwarding option and re-scroll on game change (e.g. an effect on selectedGame) instead of duplicating the markup.

findings.issue: Out-of-range page numbers are clamped for display ('Page 22 of 22') while the URL keeps ?page=999, so the address bar and results disagree.
findings.suggestion: Redirect/replace the URL to the clamped page, or leave the page param out when it's clamped to the default.

findings.issue: pageHref is a near-duplicate of updateParams's URLSearchParams merging logic, so the two can drift if a filter is ever added to only one of them.
findings.suggestion: Extract one buildSearch(current, patch) helper used by both the links and the filter handlers.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic SolidStart v2 app — query + "use server", createAsync, preload and HttpStatusCode all match the current docs, with a clean data-layer boundary and tidy components. The blocking items are small but real: failure responses are cached as null forever, the search debounce timer survives unmount and can navigate the user away from the page they just clicked, and the controlled input can swallow in-flight keystrokes. I'd ask for that round of fixes, then merge.
